newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says Q1, profits, orders rise.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says Q1, profits, orders rise.

text.p: Swedish mobile phone giant Ericsson on Friday reported a 30 percent rise in first quarter profits after financial items to 2.02 billion crowns ($262.9 million), slightly higher than the market expected.
The group also said that its mobile systems first quarter order bookings rose 22 percent and that its mobile phones and terminals sales rose almost 100 percent.

"Even measured in the increasingly stronger U.S. dollar, order bookings and net sales increased sharply during the first quarter, by 19 percent and 21 percent respectively," chief executive officer Lars Ramqvist said in a statement of results.
It said that sales in the mobile systems business rose to 12.90 billion crowns from 10.64 billion crowns.
In the infocom systems business sales were up to 9.28 billion crowns from 7.41 billion crowns and sales in mobile phones and terminals sales rose to 7.62 billion crowns from 3.83 billion crowns.
"Subscriber growth, particularly for digital systems, is very rapid throughout the world," the company said, speaking of the first quarter performance of the mobile systems business.
Net sales in infocom systems rose 19 percent for comparable units but the group said this area faced price pressures.
"As a whole, the result of the business area was weak, due partly to price pressures in the business area's major product areas and continued heavy investments in technical developments," it said.
